meta.subject: The history of the US advertising market — the count/price/admission regime
meta.corpus_ref: admarket graph (Neo4j, frozen) + p2-ad-market/data/{claims.json,eras/era-*.json}; discovery dossiers S1+S2
meta.provenance_discipline: Records provenance, not verification. No claim has been verified. Human verification status: none. Grades (A/B/C), hedges and intervals are the sources' own and are preserved. tu:era:* are SECONDARY synthesis; re-pull the backing e#- claim before any number reaches prose.
meta.evidence_classes: A=primary artefact (SEC filing, census table, FCC audit, court FOF, 10-K); B=first/second-hand documented estimate (trade series, historian compilation, settlement); C=analyst inference / vendor panel / wide-interval estimate. These map to the A-F ledger scheme; no class-F (unsourced) claim enters.
meta.gate_verdict: This ledger records provenance. No claim in it has been verified. Human verification status: none.

frame_lock.unit: One dated state of the question 'who owns the number' — who counts the audience, sets the clearing price, or admits the buyer — at one layer of the US ad transaction.
frame_lock.denominator: Per layer of the transaction (counts / prices / concentrates / targets / admits / meters / bases / units / takes), NOT per calendar year and NOT per medium.
frame_lock.window: 1833 (penny Sun) / 1869-1875 (N.W. Ayer, disclosed price) through the 2026 corpus freeze.
frame_lock.population: L0 claims (e#-/mech- ids) in the frozen 'admarket' graph that survived sourcing and grading, cross-checked against verification/verdicts-*.json; rejected ids quarantined to DEAD.

rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Thread 11: shares moved glacially (TV did not pass newspapers until 1992, ~1%); the real change was the priced unit and who counts it, not the medium.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: per calendar year on one spend series
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Thread 10/6: the Coen 1919-2007 series is non-commensurable across the 2008 seam and writes direct mail out 8 times; a single total is a basis, not a fact.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: the whole US economy / GDP as the frame
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: ad/GDP intensity peaked 1922 and the 2025 basis is non-commensurable; kept as a guard (Thread 6), not the frame.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: start at 1914 (ABC) as the founding discipline
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: 1914 was itself a correction of era-1 self-counting; starting there would smuggle in the anomaly-as-default reading the whole piece exists to overturn.

starting_hypothesis: Dated pre-derivation: the US ad market's history is a story of each new medium capturing the market from the last, culminating in a novel platform measurement/concentration crisis that Google and Meta engineered to extract rents.

load_bearing_claims.hedge: Google discloses aggregate paid-click GROWTH (~18% YoY Q4 2008) but NEVER an absolute click count, an average CPC, or a query count.
ABC founded 1914, world's first circulation auditing organisation, from a publisher-led + advertiser-led merger.
Commission rate 14.13/13.92/14.16/13.18% (1977-92) -> 10.98% (1997). 'The 15% commission survived this era largely intact; its collapse comes after it.'
US v. AAAA consent decree, final judgment 1 Feb 1956, ended collective enforcement of the 15% + recognition system.
71% of largest US national advertisers still on commission as late as 1982 — era 3 is the commission's PEAK, not its death.
Commission-basis share fell to ~10% by 2003 from 61% (1994); the collapse FOLLOWED the 1991-94 unbundling, NOT the arrival of search. [NOT_CAUSED_BY edge]
After CAB adopted Hooper's method (1944), Hooper's ratings still ran ~20% above the CAB's — the count inflated toward the vendor's paying side.
NBC+CBS RETAINED 73% ($32,046,218) of net time sales in 1938, paid 27% ($12,267,560) to 253 affiliates — knowable only because the FCC audited it.
The 15% held through the era and 'on radio it covered program production as well as media buying' — one number, two businesses.
By end-1925 AT&T sold time on its 13-station toll network at $2,600/hr (~$750k/yr) before RCA bought the business — the intermediary chain's origin.
Station reps took ~5-20% 'calculated on the amount left after the agency's 15%' — central 10 is a construction; do not harden.
A 2% cash discount on top of the 15%, 'usually omitted from take-rate comparisons' — a second, hidden plate.
People meters (Sept 1987) measured ~10% fewer prime-time viewers (CBS/ABC -13%, NBC -4%); nothing about the audience changed, only the instrument — the honest count hurt the seller.
CBS guaranteed American Tobacco $3,000/wk per Hooper point Jack Benny lost moving to CBS, Jan 1949 — a rating written into a contract.
57% of US internet ad revenue bought on pay-per-action in 2008 (up from 51% in 2007); only 39% on CPM — the direct-response meter won the medium.
Direct-response buyers spent ~$192M in 1914, ~16% of the benchmark (CI80 96-360). Pre-1975 dollars third-hand via Borden->Galbi; do not harden.
Direct mail = 24% of all US NATIONAL advertising in 1956, larger than broadcast — 'cannot be treated as a later-era phenomenon.'
National advertisers supplied 66.3% of US ad dollars in 2007, UP 4.9 pts from 61.4% (2002) — 'the opposite of what a search-eats-local story predicts.' Heads democratised, dollars did not.
Cigarette makers paid ~$225M/yr for broadcast time before the 2 Jan 1971 ban — a whole buyer class expelled by the state.
1971 was the ONLY year of the era US TV ad spend fell (-1.7%) — the mark of the cigarette ban + Prime Time Access Rule.
Classified carried 'no agency commission and no cost of preparation' (1914) — the commission-free door is 90+ years old. [EXCLUDES agency commission]
Direct mail addressed 71.1M US households one at a time in 1975, '~279,000x finer than the average unit spot TV.' Census 71.1M vs Nielsen 70.5M — different denominators, do not blend.
The best-targeted medium 'still missed 98 out of 100': a 2% response was the working definition of success. One era's rate only — do not span eras.
Overture delivered 442M intent-matched clicks in Q4 2001 'with no cookie and no profile' — the identity-free window.
Overture's 10-K benchmarked search leads against Yellow Pages. The 15.9%-on-read rate MUST NOT be compared to the 2%-on-mailed.
71% of surveyed advertisers ran Performance Max in 2025 (~75% US), up from 60%; 'no population-level figure is published.' Vendor panel — softest link, never the climax.
ATT opt-in ran ~16% at launch (May 2021) rising to ~25% by mid-2022 — the state re-separates on the demand side.
AdWords Select (20 Feb 2002): quality-weighted second-price, advertisers 'pay the lowest amount possible' — the stated neutral ideal.
Overture's founding auction was PURE first-price ('descending order of bid price'). Second-price is a Google-era artefact, not an Eden.
rGSP (2019, search) raised top-slot CPC 5.91% (PC/tablet) / 4.85% (mobile) in pre-launch experiments; 'advertisers cannot opt out.' [Mehta FOF]
Three knobs named in the Mehta FOF — squashing (internally 'Butternut Squash'), format pricing, rGSP — all 'intentional pricing'; the squashing exponent 'has never been publicly disclosed.'
Court found Google tested 5%+ text-ad raises and 'the results have been largely consistent — it can.'
Syndicated take rate rose ~9% (2002) to 24.7% (2006) then FELL to 21.3% (2008) — the ratchet reverses under competition. A pure maximizer would not let the rate fall.
Edward J. Noble paid $8M for NBC's Blue Network, 12 Oct 1943 — 'antitrust, not technology, created the third network.'
~900 AM stations (1945) -> ~2,500 (early 1950s): the one genuine deconcentration came from a supply shock the state licensed but did not design.
From 1954 the FCC capped any owner at seven TV stations (max five VHF) — a standing ceiling.
RBOC Yellow Pages sold $9,517M in 1993, exceeding radio and magazines — the state minted new sellers via the 1984 AT&T divestiture.
Google paid $26.3B in search default revenue share in 2021, the spending the court found had foreclosed competition.
TV enters the series in 1949 at $58M, 1.1% of total — the 'revolution' was glacial.
Total TV first overtook newspapers only in 1992 ($31,079M vs $30,737M, ~1%). Do not round the ~$342M away.
The Coen/McCann series UNDERSTATES internet by ~half at era end ($10,529M vs IAB/PwC $21,206M for 2007) and terminates 2007 — the instrument goes blind exactly as the new unit is born. THE MECHANISM.
US internet ad revenue $23,448M (2008) -> $294,593M (2025), 12.6x; only down year 2009 (-3%).
Direct mail took 14.5% (1949), 16.8% peak (1938), second-largest named medium most years — the channel the totals write out.
Total US ad spend 2025 ~$405B on a media-owner basis that EXCLUDES direct mail; MAGNA $398B, EMARKETER $422B — never one axis.
IRS SOI corporate ad deductions $473B (2022) vs MAGNA $325B — a $148B wedge. Corpus instruction: 'name its rail in the axis label, not the footnote.'
US ad spend reached 3.0% of GDP in 1922, the series max — capture, not expansion.
Ad/GDP fell to the 1.2% wartime floor in 1944.
US measured ad spend ~1.32% of GDP in 2025 — 'partly real and partly a change in what advertising counts.' Non-commensurable with the 1919-2007 Coen series.
IAB estimates >$26B of misallocated US media the measurement failure is moving to the wrong places.
Facebook paid $40M (Oct 2019) over overstated video watch time; plaintiffs ALLEGED up to 900% — preserve 'alleged.'
MRC suspended Nielsen's TV accreditation (Sept 2021), 2-6% undercount, VAB >=$468M — the surviving auditor bit the incumbent (residual).
Google settled Lane's Gifts (Mar 2006) for up to $90M 'mostly in advertising credits'; produced the Tuzhilin report commissioned by the defendant.
Help-wanted classified fell 91% ($8,712.6M->$786.8M); real-estate classified peaked mid-era in 2006 and fell WITH housing, NOT with search. [NOT_CAUSED_BY]
Users clicked a result on 8% of visits with an AI summary vs 15% without. CONTESTED — Google disputes the Pew study.
AI Overviews reached >2B monthly users (Jul 2025); Google's CBO says it 'monetises at approximately the same rate as classic search.' [CLAIMED_SAME_RATE_AS]
The penny Sun (3 Sep 1833) reached ~15,000/day within ~2 years — the ad-funded below-cost model. Day: 'an advantageous medium for advertisements' (anachronism flag on 'loss-leader').
Advertising supplied 64.9% of US newspapers' gross income in 1914 ($184.1M vs $99.5M) — below-cost content needs an outside payer.

Targeting entered by acquisition: Google/DoubleClick $3.1bn (13 Apr 2007), MSFT/aQuantive ~$6bn, Yahoo/Right Media $680M, WPP/24-7 $649M — bought, not built. Largest deals of the year (atypical-and-vivid).
Overture LED entering the era ($667.7M 2002 vs Google's $439.5M total) — 'not a better auction but a bigger cheque.'

dead_column.kills: 'The 15% commission died in the 1980s' — the census rate held near 14% to 1992 and 71% were still on commission in 1982.
'Search advertising killed the commission' — the mix collapse followed the 1991-94 unbundling, a NOT_CAUSED_BY edge.
'The internet/search killed classified' (single cause) — real-estate classified fell with the housing market.
'Advertising marched to the individual' — the march was to the COUNTABLE unit; the graph denies it at five eras. The identity-free query was the anomaly.
'Each new medium captured the market by killing the last' — shares moved glacially; TV passed newspapers only in 1992, by ~1%.
'TV conquered advertising / was the dominant mid-century medium' — 18.9% vs newspapers 29.5% at 1975.
'Google invented search advertising / built the per-click auction' — Overture led and built it (DID_NOT_CONTRIBUTE edge).
'Search democratised demand toward a long tail of money' — a long tail of HEADS, not dollars; national share rose.
'Self-serve / commission-free buying is a platform-era invention' — it existed by 1914.
'The middleman's cut was a stable single 15%' — a 3-4 hand stack on incompatible bases; the 15% was the smallest, most public plate.
'There is a single US ad-market total' — the 1900 total is $450M vs $542M (~20% apart); direct mail is written out 8 times.
'Platforms invented performance advertising' — direct-response was the largest single national medium for ~50 years.
'The second-price auction died' — rGSP is randomized GSP (second-price lineage); the display first-price move is a DIFFERENT market (EXCLUDES search).
'AI Overviews cut the funding click' — CONTESTED, observational cross-section, Google disputes the Pew study. Ship BOTH values as contested, never hardened.
'The 130-year subsidy is being broken' — NO corpus measure of publisher revenue dependence on search referral. Research gap.
'Response rate has been flat ~2% for a century' — only one era carries a rate; the YIELD axis cannot yet span eras.
The '5-cent AdWords bid' — e6-pricing-005 self-flags it as unsupported by either cited source. Ship the two-doors contrast WITHOUT the 5-cent figure.

omission_set_note: Corpus items deliberately NOT featured and why: the ~140 TARGETING/BUYERS/MEDIUM claims not surfaced in S2 digs (indexed, sampled, not exhausted); ~229 un-named NOT_*/NEVER_* opposition edges (only the 110 named + a sample read); the L2 theme-to-theme meta-graph (only the quarter's LIFTED{layer:2} bridges walked). None of the omitted material is known to weaken the spine; the largest self-correcting families (denominator war, targeting-was-never-the-person) are surfaced. Cherry-picking guard: the DEAD column above carries every CONTRADICTED reading a reader must be told is dead.

hypothesis_diff.before: Each new medium captured the market from the last, culminating in a novel platform crisis Google/Meta engineered to extract rents.
hypothesis_diff.after: The judged party owning the number is the DEFAULT; the independent count/price/gate was the ~90-year anomaly (1914->~2004). The platform era is a REVERSION to the pre-1914 condition at scale with no enforceable backstop, not a new medium's conquest. The mechanism is structural (drift in 1946/1950 absent any platform intent) with a birth motor (every new unit is born un-audited).
hypothesis_diff.what_changed: The frozen inventory put the seller owning the count BEFORE 1914 (self-counting) and AGAIN after 2002, with residuals (1987 people meter, 2021 MRC, take-rate reversal, Bok 1892) where the honest number hurt whoever paid for it — which the agentic 'platforms engineered it' hypothesis cannot accommodate.
